name: Shironamhin

global_influences.evidence: Shironamhin is distinguished for extended psychedelic and progressive compositions and multi-instrumental experimentation, becoming a leading band of the Bengali progressive rock genre; debut album Jahaji is explicitly classified as psychedelic rock/folk rock.

local_adaptation_notes: Formed by university students who began by jamming on campus and street corners, Shironamhin built a reputation on philosophical Bangla lyrics addressing love, grief and identity within extended, multi-part progressive/psychedelic compositions; the album 'Shironamhin Rabindranath' explicitly engages Rabindra Sangeet/Tagore's legacy, directly fusing the band's progressive-rock idiom with classical Bengali literary and musical tradition.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1996–2002): formed by Ziaur Rahman, Jewel and Bulbul Hasan as a campus/underground act; Tanzir Tuhin joined as vocalist in 2002, stabilizing the band's classic lineup. Breakthrough period (2004): debut album Jahaji established the band's psychedelic/folk-progressive rock identity. Consolidation period: Bondho Janala, Shironamhin Rabindranath, and Shironamhin Shironamhin extended national recognition, with the Rabindranath-themed album directly bridging progressive rock and classical Bengali repertoire. Legacy period (2023): 25th-anniversary live album The Only Headliner documented the band's enduring live drawing power.
concert_culture_notes: Frequently appears on major multi-band bills (e.g., alongside Warfaze and AvoidRafa per contemporaneous concert listings), and its 25th-anniversary show generated an official live album — evidence of a large, dedicated, multi-decade fan base capable of sustaining headline-level anniversary concerts.
listener_community_notes: One of the most consistently popular Bangladeshi alternative/progressive rock acts across nearly three decades, appealing to listeners drawn to philosophical lyricism and genre-blending (psychedelic, folk, symphonic) rather than a single fixed style; frequently referenced alongside Meghdol and Shunno as a pillar of the alternative rock listener ecosystem.
